1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16.

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).

2.q: הִנָּבֵא֙ וְ⁠אָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה הֵילִ֖ילוּ הָ֥הּ לַ⁠יּֽוֹם
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [prophesy and tell them that the Lord Yahweh says that they should wail in grief about how terrible that day will be]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4.

Yahweh is telling the people to use a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of grief and dread. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How terrible that day will be]

3.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [You should wail because a day is near]

Yahweh is using **a day is near for Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time is near when Yahweh will judge and punish people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the time is near when Yahweh will judge and punish people]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the time of his judgment were **a day of cloud**. It means that it will be a dark and gloomy time of disaster. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a day of distress and disaster]

The implication is that this will be a time when Yahweh judges and punishes the **nations**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [it will be a time of judgment for the nations]

4.note: Here, **a sword** represents “an enemy army that fights with swords.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And an enemy army will invade Egypt]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **anguish**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the people in Cush will be greatly distressed]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:7.
The pronoun **they** refers to the enemy soldiers who invade Egypt. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the enemy soldiers take her multitude]
See how you translated this same phrase in Ezekiel 29:19. Alternate translation: [and they take away all her people] or [and they take away all her possessions]

The expression **are torn down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it is clear from the context that the enemy soldiers do it. Alternate translation: [and the enemy soldiers tear down her foundations]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if Egypt were a building whose **foundations** could be **torn down**. It means that the things that make Egypt strong and stable will be destroyed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the things that make her strong are destroyed]

5.note: The words **Cush**, **Put**, **Lud**, and **Cub** are the names of places.

The implication is that **all the mixed company** were foreign people allied with Egypt. This could mean: (1) foreign soldiers whom Egypt hired to fight in its army. Alternate translation: [and all the foreign soldiers whom Egypt hired] or (2) the mixed population of foreign people who lived in Egypt. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and all the foreigners living in Egypt]

The implication is that **the sons of the land of the covenant** were people allied with Egypt. This could mean: (1) people from Judah, the land with which Yahweh had made his covenant, who were living in Egypt. Alternate translation: [and the people from Judah, the land of Yahweh’s covenant, who are allied] or (2) people from countries that had made a treaty with Egypt. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and people who are allied]
See how you translated this expression in 25:13.

6.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the nations that help Egypt were **supports** that hold Egypt up the way posts hold up a building. It means that these allied nations will be defeated and will no longer be able to help Egypt. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the allies of Egypt will be defeated]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if **the pride of her strength** were something that could **go down** from a high place. It means that the strength that Egypt was proud of will be weakened and destroyed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the strength that she is proud of will be destroyed]
See how you translated the similar expression in 29:10.

Yahweh is using **the declaration of the Lord Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

7.q: וְ⁠נָשַׁ֕מּוּ בְּ⁠ת֖וֹךְ אֲרָצ֣וֹת נְשַׁמּ֑וֹת וְ⁠עָרָ֕י⁠ו בְּ⁠תוֹךְ־עָרִ֥ים נַחֲרָב֖וֹת תִּֽהְיֶֽינָה
7.note: See how you translated these same phrases in Ezekiel 29:12.

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:7.

The expression **are broken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it is clear from the context that Yahweh will do it. Alternate translation: [and I break all of her helpers]

Yahweh is speaking as if Egypt’s **helpers** were objects that could be **broken**. It means that the nations that help Egypt will be completely defeated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and all of her helpers are completely defeated]

9.note: Here, **my face** represents “my presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from my presence]

The implication is that the people of **Cush** felt secure because they were far from the fighting and did not think that they would be harmed. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to make the people of Cush tremble, who felt secure because they were far away from the fighting]

Yahweh is using **the day of Egypt** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the time when Egypt is punished.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the time when Egypt is punished]

The pronoun **it** refers to **the day of Egypt**, the time when Yahweh will punish Egypt. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for behold, the day of Egypt is coming]

Yahweh is using **behold it is coming** as a common expression of the culture to mean “it is certainly going to happen.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [look, it is about to happen] or [it is surely going to happen]

10.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4.

Here, **hand** represents “power” or “action.” Yahweh means that he will use Nebuchadnezzar and his army to do this. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [through the army of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon]

11.note: See how you translated this phrase in 28:7.

The expression **are being brought** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it is clear from the context that Yahweh is doing it. Alternate translation: [are the ones whom I am bringing to destroy the land]

Yahweh is using **draw out their swords against Egypt** as a common expression of the culture to mean “attack Egypt.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they will attack Egypt]

Yahweh says **fill the land with the slain** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means that the enemy soldiers will kill a very large number of people throughout Egypt. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [and kill a great many people throughout the land]

12.note: The implication is that **the streams** are the Nile River and the channels that branch off from it, which provided water for the land. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And I will make the Nile River and its channels dry ground]

Yahweh is speaking as if giving Egypt over to its enemies were a way to **sell** property. It means that he will put the land under the control of **evil ones**, that is, cruel foreign people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will let evil people control the land and people]

Yahweh is using **the land and its fullness** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the land and everything in it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the land and all that is in it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:21.
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:15.

13.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will completely do away with the worthless idols from Memphis]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **prince**. He means princes in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and … any princes]

Here, **the land of Egypt** represents “the people who live in Egypt.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And I will put fear in the people who live in Egypt]

14.note: The word **Pathros** is the name of a region in southern Egypt, and the words **Zoan** and **On** are the names of cities in Egypt.

Yahweh is using **do judgments in On** as a common expression of the culture to mean “punish the people of On.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will punish those who live in On]

15.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **wrath** were a liquid that he could **pour out** on a city. It means that he will punish the city of **Sin** severely because he is very angry with its people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And in my anger I will severely punish Sin]

Yahweh is not distinguishing this city of **Sin** from another city named Sin that is not **the fortress of Egypt**. Yahweh is reminding his hearers that Sin is the strong city that protects Egypt. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [Sin, which is the strong city that protects Egypt]
The word **Sin** is the name of a city in Egypt. This name is not related to the English word “sin.”

Yahweh is speaking as if the people of On were something that he could **cut off**. It means that he will kill **the multitude of On**, that is, the many people who live there. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will destroy the many people who live in On]

16.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **writhe** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Sin will writhe in terrible agony]

Yahweh is speaking of **Sin** as if it were a living thing that could **writhe** in pain. He means that the people of Sin will suffer great pain and distress. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people of Sin will suffer terrible pain]
See how you translated this name in 30:15.

The expression **for being broken open** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it is clear from the context that enemy soldiers will break through the walls of On. Alternate translation: [and enemy soldiers will break through the walls of On]

The implication is that enemies will attack **Memphis**. This could mean: (1) that they will attack the city every day. Alternate translation: [and enemies will attack Memphis day after day] or (2) that they will attack the city openly in broad daylight. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and enemies will attack Memphis during the day]

17.note: The words **Aven** and **Pi Beseth** are the names of cities in Egypt.

Some ancient manuscripts read **Aven** which could also mean “evil.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “On” which is generally identified as Heliopolis. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT. Alternate translation: [Evil young men] or [The young men of On]

This could mean that the pronoun **they** refers to: (1) the people of the cities of **Aven and Pi Beseth**. Alternate translation: [and the people of those cities will go] or (2) the **young men** of those cities who are not killed by the sword. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the young men of those cities who are not killed will go]

18.note: The word **Tahpanhes** is the name of a city in Egypt.

Yahweh is speaking as if the time of disaster were a time when **the day will grow dark**. It means that it will be a time of great trouble and sorrow for the people of Tahpanhes. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [there will be a time of great trouble]

Yahweh is speaking as if Egypt’s power over other nations were **yokes** that Egypt had put on them, like the wooden bars that people put on the necks of oxen. It means that he will end Egypt’s power to control other nations. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when I end there Egypt’s control over other nations]

Yahweh puts the pronoun **She** at the beginning of the sentence for emphasis. If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **She** with the information about **her** in a single clause. Alternate translation: [A cloud will cover her]

Yahweh is speaking as if the towns and villages around the city were the city’s **daughters**. It means that the people of those surrounding communities will be taken captive. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the people of her surrounding towns will go into captivity]

19.note: See how you translated this expression in 6:7.

20.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **eleventh**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year eleven]

21.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).

Here, **arm** represents “military power.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the military power of Pharaoh the king of Egypt]

21.q: לֹֽא־חֻ֠בְּשָׁה לָ⁠תֵ֨ת רְפֻא֜וֹת לָ⁠שׂ֥וּם חִתּ֛וּל לְ⁠חָבְשָׁ֥⁠הּ לְ⁠חָזְקָ֖⁠הּ לִ⁠תְפֹּ֥שׂ בֶּ⁠חָֽרֶב
21.note: Yahweh is speaking as if Pharaoh’s military power were a broken arm that **has not been bound up** and that no one has treated with **medicines** or **a bandage** therefore it cannot **grasp** a **sword**. It means that Egypt’s army has not recovered from its defeat and will not become strong again. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [no one has helped his defeated army to recover so it is still weak]

The expression **has not been bound up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could use an indefinite expression such as “no one.” Alternate translation: [no one has bound it up]

22.q: לָ⁠כֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהֹוִ֗ה הִנְ⁠נִי֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם
22.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Therefore I, the Lord Yahweh, declare that I am against Pharaoh the king of Egypt]

**Behold me** is an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to act against Pharaoh the king of Egypt]

The expression **the broken one** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it is clear from the context that Yahweh had already broken this arm. Alternate translation: [the strong one and the one that I already broke]

The implication is that **the strong one** is the arm that Pharaoh can still use and **the broken one** is the arm that Yahweh has already broken. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the one he can still use and the one that I have already broken]

Yahweh is speaking as if Pharaoh were a warrior who would drop the **sword** from **his hand**. It means that Pharaoh will no longer be able to fight in battle. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will make him unable to fight in battle any longer]

23.q: וַ⁠הֲפִצוֹתִ֥י אֶת מִצְרַ֖יִם בַּ⁠גּוֹיִ֑ם וְ⁠זֵרִיתִ֖⁠ם בָּ⁠אֲרָצֽוֹת
23.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 29:12.

Here, **Egypt** represents “the people of Egypt.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations]

24.note: Yahweh is speaking as if he would put his own **sword** in the hand of the king of Babylon. It means that he will use the king of Babylon to carry out his judgment. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will enable him to punish Egypt on my behalf]

Here, **arms** represents the power or military strength of the king of Babylon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And I will increase the power of the king of]

Yahweh is speaking as if Pharaoh were a man who has been wounded so badly that he is about to die and who would **groan the groanings of a slain one**. It means that Pharaoh will suffer terribly and be completely defeated. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will be completely defeated and cry out in pain]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

25.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:7.

The pronoun **he** refers to the king of Babylon, and the pronoun **it** refers to Yahweh’s sword. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the king of Babylon stretches my sword out against the land of Egypt]

25.q: בְּ⁠תִתִּ֤⁠י חַרְבִּ⁠י֙ בְּ⁠יַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל & וְ⁠נָטָ֥ה אוֹתָ֖⁠הּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
25.note: Yahweh is speaking as if his judgment were a **sword** that he places in the hand of the king of Babylon, who then stretches it out against Egypt. It means that Yahweh will give the king of Babylon the power and authority to carry out his judgment by attacking Egypt. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when I empower the king of Babylon to carry out my judgment and he attacks the land of Egypt]

26.q: וַ⁠הֲפִצוֹתִ֤י אֶת־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בַּ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם וְ⁠זֵרִיתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖⁠ם בָּ⁠אֲרָצ֑וֹת
26.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 30:23.
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:7.
